1	/**
2	 * AC 91-79A Table 3-1 — Landing Distance Factors.
3	 *
4	 * Source: FAA Advisory Circular 91-79A, "Runway Overrun Prevention", Table 3-1.
5	 *   https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/advisory_circulars/index.cfm/go/document.information/documentID/1041345
6	 *
7	 * Table 3-1 is a 4 × 7 matrix. Rows are aircraft propulsion category; columns
8	 * are runway condition code (RCC) per FAA TALPA. Values are the unfactored-to-
9	 * factored multiplier the AC recommends applying to POH landing-distance data.
10	 *
11	 * The same factors are also applied to the takeoff side of the dispatch
12	 * Performance step in this app — historically the wizard hardcoded 1.5× for
13	 * takeoff and 1.43× for landing, which under-states the margin for any non-dry
14	 * condition. (Per the Asana ticket that introduced this module: those values
15	 * are not from Table 3-1 — the table starts at 1.67× even for a dry runway.)
16	 *
17	 * ⚠️ Safety note — partial table.
18	 *   Only the **reciprocating** row is populated below, sourced verbatim from
19	 *   the originating Asana ticket (1214622594542107). The remaining three
20	 *   propulsion categories (turboprop, turbojet without reverse, turbojet with
21	 *   reverse) are intentionally absent until a human verifies the values
22	 *   directly from the AC PDF. Hilo's training fleet is overwhelmingly
23	 *   reciprocating piston, so shipping reciprocating alone solves the primary
24	 *   safety gap (a recip on a contaminated runway needs up to 5.1× per Table
25	 *   3-1; the app currently applies 1.43×). Exposing the other three
26	 *   categories with unverified values would re-create the bug the ticket is
27	 *   trying to fix.
28	 *
29	 *   Phase 2: a follow-up ticket should populate the remaining rows from the
30	 *   AC PDF, then add the categories to CATEGORY_OPTIONS so the dropdown
31	 *   surfaces them. The type union below already includes all four categories
32	 *   so the expansion is purely additive.
33	 *
34	 *   When the FAA revises the AC, update both this constant and the unit tests
35	 *   in `src/__tests__/dispatch/sdf-table.test.ts`.
36	 */
37	
38	export const AC_91_79A_PDF_URL =
39	  'https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/advisory_circulars/index.cfm/go/document.information/documentID/1041345';
40	
41	export type AircraftCategory =
42	  | 'reciprocating'
43	  | 'turboprop'
44	  | 'turbojet_no_rev'
45	  | 'turbojet_rev';
46	
47	export type RunwayConditionCode = '6' | '5G' | '5S' | '4' | '3' | '2' | '1';
48	
49	export interface CategoryOption {
50	  value: AircraftCategory;
51	  label: string;
52	}
53	
54	export interface RccOption {
55	  value: RunwayConditionCode;
56	  label: string;
57	  shortLabel: string;
58	}
59	
60	/**
61	 * Categories currently exposed in the UI dropdown. Reciprocating only until
62	 * Phase 2 verifies the remaining rows of Table 3-1 from the AC PDF.
63	 */
64	export const CATEGORY_OPTIONS: readonly CategoryOption[] = [
65	  { value: 'reciprocating', label: 'Reciprocating' },
66	];
67	
68	export const RCC_OPTIONS: readonly RccOption[] = [
69	  { value: '6', label: '6 — Dry', shortLabel: 'Dry' },
70	  { value: '5G', label: '5 — Grooved / PFC, Good', shortLabel: 'Grooved Good' },
71	  { value: '5S', label: '5 — Smooth, Good', shortLabel: 'Smooth Good' },
72	  { value: '4', label: '4 — Good to Medium', shortLabel: 'Good-Medium' },
73	  { value: '3', label: '3 — Medium', shortLabel: 'Medium' },
74	  { value: '2', label: '2 — Medium to Poor', shortLabel: 'Medium-Poor' },
75	  { value: '1', label: '1 — Poor', shortLabel: 'Poor' },
76	];
77	
78	/**
79	 * AC 91-79A Table 3-1, partial. Only the reciprocating row is populated; see
80	 * the safety note in the file header.
81	 */
82	export const AC_91_79A_TABLE_3_1: Partial<
83	  Record<AircraftCategory, Record<RunwayConditionCode, number>>
84	> = {
85	  reciprocating: {
86	    '6': 1.67,
87	    '5G': 2.3,
88	    '5S': 2.6,
89	    '4': 2.8,
90	    '3': 3.2,
91	    '2': 4.0,
92	    '1': 5.1,
93	  },
94	};
95	
96	/**
97	 * Look up the SDF for a (category, RCC) pair. Returns `null` when the row is
98	 * not yet populated in the partial table — callers should fall back to the
99	 * student's manual override or surface a "values pending verification" note
100	 * rather than silently using a wrong number.
101	 */
102	export function lookupSdf(
103	  category: AircraftCategory,
104	  rcc: RunwayConditionCode,
105	): number | null {
106	  const row = AC_91_79A_TABLE_3_1[category];
107	  if (!row) return null;
108	  return row[rcc];
109	}
110	
111	/**
112	 * Best-effort heuristic for pre-filling Aircraft Category from the equipment
113	 * record. Only categories present in CATEGORY_OPTIONS are returned, so the
114	 * dropdown selection is always valid for the current phase. Defaults to
115	 * 'reciprocating' (which is the only currently-exposed option).
116	 *
117	 * `engineType` on the equipment table stores "Single Engine" / "Multi Engine"
118	 * (count, not propulsion), so this is mostly a placeholder until Phase 2
119	 * populates the rest of Table 3-1.
120	 */
121	export function inferAircraftCategory(
122	  _engineModel?: string | null,
123	  _engineType?: string | null,
124	): AircraftCategory {
125	  return 'reciprocating';
126	}
127	
128	/**
129	 * Pre-fill the RCC dropdown from the existing Surface dropdown. The student
130	 * may still override — this is a default, not a constraint.
131	 *
132	 * Mapping rationale:
133	 *   Dry Pavement   → 6   (matches the AC's Dry definition)
134	 *   Wet Pavement   → 5S  (Smooth Good — conservative; airports with grooved /
135	 *                         PFC pavement should manually pick 5G)
136	 *   Grass (Dry)    → 4   (treated as Good-to-Medium per typical GA practice)
137	 *   Soft / Muddy   → 2   (Medium-to-Poor)
138	 */
139	export function inferRccFromSurface(surface: string): RunwayConditionCode {
140	  switch (surface) {
141	    case 'dry':
142	      return '6';
143	    case 'wet':
144	      return '5S';
145	    case 'grass':
146	      return '4';
147	    case 'soft':
148	      return '2';
149	    default:
150	      return '6';
151	  }
152	}
153	
154	/**
155	 * Resolve the Safety Distance Factor to apply to POH ground roll / over-50ft
156	 * distances. If the override is enabled and parses to a positive number, that
157	 * value wins; otherwise we use the table-derived factor. Returns null when no
158	 * factor can be determined (table cell missing, override empty, etc.) so the
159	 * UI can refuse to render a misleading "all clear" margin.
160	 */
161	export function resolveSdf(input: {
162	  category: AircraftCategory | '';
163	  rcc: RunwayConditionCode | '';
164	  overrideEnabled: boolean;
165	  overrideValue: string;
166	}): number | null {
167	  if (input.overrideEnabled) {
168	    const parsed = Number.parseFloat(input.overrideValue);
169	    if (Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0) return parsed;
170	    return null;
171	  }
172	  if (!input.category || !input.rcc) return null;
173	  return lookupSdf(input.category, input.rcc);
174	}
